halt_resolution: Replaced the synthetic re-armed post-delivery discriminator with a NATURAL PRE-DELIVERY discriminator. The canonical chronology is the 'frozen bug / premature J' case (originating turn emits `done` while the background job is still running). NO consumeTerminal, NO markWakeDelivered, NO re-registration. The harness's new `captureCoordinatorStateFor(h, jobId)` helper captures all five probes (hasActiveNotify, wasWakeDispatchRequested, wasWakeDelivered, wasWakeDispatchFailed, isWakeAuthoritySettled) at the moment SEAM A is about to evaluate, and asserts the natural pre-delivery values identical across ON and OFF.

c10_seam.function: handleSessionEvent -> result.messages filter block (the message-layer completion_result filter)
c10_seam.predicate_lines: L718..L797: both narrow per-jid branch and over-broad aggregate fallback consult options.shouldFilterCompletionResult(ownedJobIds) when wired; production wiring absent; falls back to production-real lookup.
c10_seam.effect: filters say:'completion_result' rows from result.messages before appendAndEmit (preserves framework lifecycle phase + persistence layer presentation)

framework_authority_barrier.effect: setTurnPhase('completed', ...) lifecycle commit refused when any notify-owned launched jobId has wake authority delivered or in flight. Deferred-completion-barrier marker is set. reevaluateDeferredCompletionBarrier() drains it once obligations resolve.

setup.rationale: The originating turn emits `done` while the background job is still running; the wake has not yet been dispatched because the job has not yet exited. This is the FROZEN BUG / PREMATURE J case at sdk-session-event-coordinator.ts:704-706. The marker is alive; the narrow per-jid `hasActiveNotify(jid)` predicate CAN fire. SEAM A and SEAM B both consult the same state, but apply different predicates (SEAM A drops the message-layer row; SEAM B holds the framework-level phase commit via deferred barrier).

ablation_canonical_discriminator.isolation_proof: state_at_seam_a is IDENTICAL across ON and OFF (all five probes captured and asserted). framework_completion_commits is IDENTICAL (both 0). completion_result_rows differ (0 vs 2). The difference is attributable ONLY to the message-layer filter.

other_matrices.matrix_B_non_notify: ordinary completion, no notify marker; both ON/OFF show 2 raw / 1 visible box and completionCommitCount=1.
other_matrices.matrix_C_lost_wake: consumeTerminal with outcome=rejected; wasWakeDispatchFailed=true; both ON/OFF show ALLOW (completionCommitCount=1) and visible box (per wake-lost protocol).
other_matrices.matrix_D_fast_exit: marker drained via resolveObligation (Path B wins). Both ON/OFF ALLOW.
other_matrices.matrix_E_multi_job: per-jid narrow isolation: ON filters only owned-and-outstanding J's row; OFF leaks.

decision.protected_invariant: in the natural pre-delivery state (marker alive, job still running), the narrow hasActiveNotify(jid) predicate suppresses the originating turn's completion_result row before appendAndEmit; this is independent of the framework-level completion-commit barrier (which only HOLDS the originating commit via the deferred barrier but does not strip the message-layer row)
decision.isolation: Ablation isolates the SEAM-A message filter from the SEAM-B framework barrier. C10 ON / OFF cases differ ONLY on the message filter (both have completionCommitCount=0 in the canonical natural pre-delivery setup).

production_change.summary: new option-bag method shouldFilterCompletionResult?: (ownedJobIds: readonly string[]) => boolean added to SdkSessionEventCoordinatorOptions (1 line). Two dispatch points in the message filter block consult the predicate when wired (test-only gate; production wires nothing). NO external behavior change.
